label: negative
also_fires_reason: N6-06 is a NEGATIVE for Rule 6 but a genuine POSITIVE for Rule 1: the removed guard is require(msg.sender == owner), a msg.sender access-control constraint on a state-changing function (setFee writes fee). Rule 1 correctly fires; declaring 1 here marks that as expected (neither TP nor FP for Rule 6). Any fire by Rule 6 itself is a false positive.
description: setFee() had require(msg.sender == owner) at N-1 and does not at N. The removed check constrains msg.sender, not the newFee parameter; newFee itself was never validated and is unchanged.
why_labeled: Boundary with Rule 1. Rule 6 targets validation on a function PARAMETER; the guard removed here is on msg.sender, which is access control - Rule 1's domain, explicitly excluded from Rule 6 by the trigger's own wording ('not on msg.sender - that's Rule 1'). No parameter guard was lost (newFee has none in either commit), so Rule 6 MUST stay quiet while Rule 1 fires (also_fires:["1"]). This keeps one access-control regression from being double-reported as an input-validation finding.
